result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers correctly identify proportional figures as the cause and give the same pasteable tabular-nums fix while keeping Gill Sans. B makes a misleading claim that font-feature-settings: "tnum" gives a guaranteed result, but it depends on the font in exactly the same way. B also asserts some doubtful things about Calibri and the bold weight. A handles font support more honestly and adds a practical way to check it in DevTools. B is slightly stronger on noting that alignment and padding still matter. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers correctly identify proportional figures as the cause and give the same paste-ready tabular-nums fix while keeping Gill Sans. A wrongly suggests that font-feature-settings: "tnum" can guarantee the result: it cannot add a feature the font lacks. A also adds a doubtful claim that bold makes the problem worse. B handles fallback fonts more honestly, offering humanist webfonts that support tabular figures and a DevTools check to confirm which font is rendering.
